subject: health

location.unitTitle: Media, Technology, and Digital Influence on Health
location.courseTitle: Health II: Mental Health and Community Wellness

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the private-safe task without disclosing medical history, diagnosis, body measurements, or sexual history.
Use a fictional scenario when offered and identify a trusted adult or qualified professional where appropriate.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain algorithmic feeds, engagement incentives, and health misinformation in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of influencer marketing, sponsorship disclosure, and undisclosed advertising.
Apply appearance filters, edited imagery, and body-image pressure in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving evaluating a health claim: source, evidence, plausibility, and incentive; correct it and explain why.
Connect privacy, data, and health information shared online with digital wellbeing: notification load, sleep, and attention. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Take apart three fictional but realistic health posts: identify the claim, the incentive, the evidence actually offered, and what a reliable source says instead. Write the correction you would actually post.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated accuracy of health information criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated evidence and reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill application criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated checking and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Media, Technology, and Digital Influence on Health?
